summary:
SpaceMedx is a modular health monitoring and decision-support platform designed to support astronauts and crews operating in isolated, remote, and resource-constrained environments.

The platform combines wearable sensors, a cross-platform mobile application, local data processing, and a centralized monitoring architecture to collect, visualize, and manage physiological and mission-related health information.
Our functional Mobile HUB supports local data acquisition, storage, visualization, and synchronization with a central database. The system is designed to operate with intermittent connectivity, allowing crew members to retain access to their health information when communication with Earth is limited.

SpaceMedx introduces a scalable architecture for future health trend analysis, risk detection, emergency support, and AI-assisted recommendations.

Starting with research and analog missions, our vision is to evolve SpaceMedx into an autonomous health-support platform for space stations, lunar habitats, and future Mars exploration missions.

Our mission: Making health monitoring more autonomous, accessible, and resilient — on Earth and beyond.
details:
The Challenge: Healthcare Beyond Earth

Human space exploration creates extraordinary healthcare challenges. Astronauts operate in isolated and harsh environments where medical resources are limited, communication may be delayed, and immediate consultation with Earth-based specialists may not be possible.

Long-duration missions require more than collecting health data. Crew members need tools that help them understand physiological changes, recognize emerging risks, and communicate relevant information to authorized medical personnel.

SpaceMedx addresses this challenge through an extensible health monitoring architecture designed for autonomous local operation and asynchronous remote collaboration.

Our Solution

SpaceMedx connects wearable health monitoring technologies with a modular software ecosystem consisting of three principal components:

1. Mobile Health HUB

A cross-platform application for Android and iOS that supports physiological data acquisition, local storage, visualization, and processing.

The HUB is designed to work with simulated datasets, commercial wearable technologies, and future custom-developed smart sensor garments.

2. Central Health Monitoring Platform

A modular backend architecture based on Python, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL, combined with a React, TypeScript and web portal.

The architecture supports secure data synchronization, longitudinal health monitoring, user management, mission and team organization, and controlled access to sensitive health information.

3. Autonomous Health Intelligence

The decision-support layer is progressively introduce deterministic monitoring rules, individual baseline analysis, anomaly detection, validated machine learning, and advanced AI capabilities.

The objective is to support early identification of potential health risks and provide understandable, actionable information without requiring continuous communication with Earth.

How It Works

SpaceMedx follows a hybrid onboard/ground operational model.

Physiological and behavioral data are collected through wearable devices and other compatible sources. The Mobile HUB stores and processes information locally, allowing continued monitoring during connectivity interruptions.

When communication becomes available, selected data can be synchronized with the central platform, where authorized personnel can review individual health trends, mission-level monitoring information, and relevant alerts.

The architecture also includes a planned emergency access mechanism enabling designated on-site team leaders to access assigned crew members' health information under controlled, auditable conditions.

Technologies and Development

The SpaceMedx technology stack includes:

  • Flutter and Dart for cross-platform mobile development.
  • Python and FastAPI for backend services.
  • PostgreSQL for centralized structured data storage.
  • React, TypeScript, and web interface.
  • Commercial wearable ecosystems and simulated physiological data sources.
  • Modular interfaces for future biomedical sensors and smart garments.

Both the Mobile HUB, the central backend, protected web portal, and autonomous decision-support capabilities are functionally available. They form part of the established architecture and ongoing development roadmap.

Innovation and Creativity

SpaceMedx combines several important principles:

Local-first operation: Health monitoring should remain available even when communication infrastructure is unreliable.

Individualized monitoring: Future analytical functions will consider personal physiological baselines rather than relying exclusively on population-level thresholds.

Mission-aware design: The platform is structured around crews, missions, teams, and operational responsibilities.

Modular integration: Commercial wearable technologies can provide an accessible starting point, while specialized space-compatible sensors can be integrated later.

Real-time and historical data integration: Already existing data sets about missions, and human subjects are reused for data processing and assessment, and combined with acquired real data for visualisation.

Progressive autonomy: Decision support will evolve from transparent deterministic rules toward validated machine learning and advanced AI.

Controlled emergency access: The architecture considers the need to balance medical confidentiality with emergency crew safety.

Intended Impact

Our initial target environments are research projects, analog space missions, and isolated operational teams.

Longer-term applications include space stations, lunar habitats, and future interplanetary exploration.

The same technology principles may also benefit terrestrial environments such as remote research stations, polar expeditions, offshore facilities, disaster-response operations, and other settings where access to healthcare professionals is limited.

SpaceMedx aims to improve health awareness, support earlier recognition of physiological deterioration, and provide a scalable foundation for future autonomous health-support technologies.

Responsible Development

SpaceMedx is being developed with attention to privacy, cybersecurity, human oversight, interoperability, and the validation requirements associated with health-related software.

The current platform is a research and technology-development solution, not a clinically validated medical diagnostic system. Future clinical or mission-critical functionality will require appropriate verification, validation, and regulatory assessment.

SpaceMedx represents a step toward a future in which intelligent health monitoring accompanies humans wherever exploration takes them.
